It's an even direr outlook for Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE), one of the central bank's preferred inflation measures. PCE accounts for the substitution effect (i.e., consumers trading down to cheaper goods) and includes third-party payments made on behalf of consumers. This makes it a more encompassing inflationary measure than the CPI.

The Inflation Nowcasting tool is forecasting an annualized PCE of 3.78% in August and 3.97% in September, up from a reported 3.7% in July.
